chapter.title: The Painter
chapter.note: Rebuilt on 6 November 2026 at flowchart-node level from the PowerPyx 100% chart (44 nodes) and the game’s text (detroitbecometext template and string table), with the Fandom wiki’s chapter page and transcript. ARRIVING HOME → DROP OFF PACKAGE → WAKE CARL → (CARL NOTICES MARKUS’ CLOTHES, after the protesters in Shades of Color) → SERVE BREAKFAST → FIND SOMETHING TO DO → PLAY CHESS (WIN / LOSE / DRAW) or READ BOOK (Plato / Shakespeare / Keats) or PLAY PIANO (four moods) → TAKE CARL TO THE STUDIO → PAINT SOMETHING YOU SEE (three subjects) → PAINT FROM THE HEART (ANDROIDS / HUMANITY / IDENTITY, four feelings each) → LEO INTRUDED TO ASK FOR MONEY, the only ending. Optional: the magazine (two covers) and the birds. The template’s live prompts (WIN / LOSE / DRAW and the three follow-ups, LIKE / DON’T LIKE / NO OPINION) are all offered; the cut FACTUAL / REASSURING prompt is not. No probability, relationship, public-opinion or instability change anywhere. Cross-chapter: clothesTorn in; the pastime (painterActivity) and the painting (painterTheme, painterFeeling) out, for Night of the Soul. Researched in docs/research/chapters/ch05-the-painter.md. Story 1.9.11: Waiting without an activity reaches the existing speech and studio instruction (docs/research/video-evidence/ch05/ch05-08-Girel6zYFVo-02-32.png and ch05-08-Girel6zYFVo-02-52.png). No precise idle timer is inferred.

decisions.title: Arriving Home (checkpoint) and Drop Off Package
decisions.context: Markus comes home from Bellini Paints at 09:58 on November 5, 2038: “Alarm deactivated. Welcome home, Markus.” He leaves Carl’s package on the hutch in the hall and hangs up his coat; the next objective is to wake Carl upstairs.

options.label: Scripted, no choice
options.effect: The start node and checkpoint, then the main-line node DROP OFF PACKAGE (objective DEPOSIT PACKAGE). The hall mirror shows a torn or an unscathed shirt.

decisions.gate: Chapter start, after A New Home.
decisions.note: Chart nodes ARRIVING HOME (checkpoint) and DROP OFF PACKAGE. No icon on either.

benchmark.note: One narrated event covers both nodes; the mirror sentence appears when clothesTorn is set. One fact; no stat change.

decisions.title: Read the living-room magazine
decisions.context: A magazine with two covers on the table in front of the living-room TV: Century, “The North Pole - Why Russia Wants It” (thirium minerals under the Arctic ice; Warren: “Russia has no business in the Arctic”), and Detroit Today, “Life Found on Titan!” (microorganisms under Titan’s ice; CyberLife’s space-faring androids).

options.label: READ “NORTH POLE RUSSIA”
options.effect: Century: the Arctic dispute over thirium minerals. BOOKWORM No. 2.

options.label: READ “LIFE ON TITAN”
options.effect: Detroit Today: life found on Titan. BOOKWORM No. 27.

decisions.gate: Optional, from arrival until the pastime is chosen.
decisions.note: Two optional chart nodes in the side group drawn under WAKE CARL, with no line to the main path. No public-opinion effect.

benchmark.note: A media scene before waking Carl (R05); whatever was left unread is offered again with the TV after breakfast (R05b). Facts go to Markus’s knowledge; no stat change.

decisions.title: Activate Birds
decisions.context: In the hall, a cage of two small robot songbirds; Markus can switch each on with its button, and they chirp at each other.
decisions.gate: Optional, before or after waking Carl.
decisions.note: Optional side node in the same group as the magazine (wiki: “found in main lobby”).

benchmark.note: A two-option decision before going upstairs; in the game it can also be done later. No stat change.

decisions.title: Wake Carl
decisions.context: Markus draws the curtains, reports the time and weather (“It’s 10 AM … partly cloudy, 54°, 80% humidity”) and gives Carl his injection (“Show me your arm please, Carl.” “No!”). Carl: “Humans are such a fragile machine… They break down so quickly…”

options.label: Scripted, no choice
options.effect: Main-line node; objectives WAKE CARL UPSTAIRS and ADMINISTER CARL’S MEDICINE.

benchmark.note: A narrated event quoting the template. One fact; no stat change.

decisions.title: Carl notices Markus’ clothes
decisions.context: If the protesters harassed Markus in Shades of Color, Carl sees the damage: “Hey. What happened to your clothes?” Markus: “Oh, it’s nothing… Just some demonstrators in the street, Carl…” Carl: “What a bunch of idiots… I hope they didn’t harm you…”

options.label: Scripted, no choice
options.effect: Plays only after PROTESTERS HARASS MARKUS. A reply prompt FACTUAL / REASSURING was cut from the game.

decisions.gate: Only when the protesters harassed Markus in Shades of Color.
decisions.note: Chart node with the triangle icon (unlocked by an earlier chapter).

benchmark.note: An event gated on clothesTorn (set in Shades of Color, M00f). One fact; no stat change.

decisions.title: Serve Breakfast
decisions.context: Markus bathes Carl and takes him down; on the way Carl hears about his retrospective at the Museum of Modern Art (the gallery director left four messages) and asks for news of Leo (none; “No, don’t bother”). Bacon and eggs; “Television.” The CTN news reports the Arctic crisis (“never been so close to a Third World War”). “Why don’t you find something to do while I finish my breakfast?”

options.label: Scripted, no choice
options.effect: Main-line node. The TV report is optional and has no effect.

decisions.note: Main-line node; the broadcast is not a chart node and moves no stat.

benchmark.note: An event quoting the template (two facts), then a media scene with the TV and any magazine cover left unread. No stat change.

decisions.title: Find Something To Do (checkpoint)
decisions.context: While Carl finishes his breakfast, Markus can choose chess, a book, piano, or wait without an activity. Story 1.9.11: Waiting without an activity reaches the existing speech and studio instruction (docs/research/video-evidence/ch05/ch05-08-Girel6zYFVo-02-32.png and ch05-08-Girel6zYFVo-02-52.png). No precise idle timer is inferred.

options.label: PLAY CHESS
options.effect: Speed chess with Carl; Night of the Soul: LOOK AT THE CHESSBOARD if Carl is alive.

options.label: READ BOOK
options.effect: A book Carl recommended; Night of the Soul: BROWSE BOOKS.

options.label: PLAY PIANO
options.effect: A piece on Carl’s piano; Night of the Soul: PLAY PIANO.

options.label: WAIT / DO NOTHING
options.effect: Carl finishes breakfast; the same speech and studio instruction follow. painterActivity none; no pastime unlocked later.

decisions.gate: Main line; at most one pastime per playthrough.
decisions.note: Checkpoint and choice group. The wiki and transcript also allow doing nothing (Carl gives the same speech); the chart draws no line for it.

benchmark.note: Four options, including waiting without an activity; stored as painterActivity. No stat change.

decisions.title: Speed chess
decisions.context: Carl: “Fancy a game of chess?” “Speed chess.” Markus decides the final move.

options.label: WIN
options.effect: Carl: “That’s what I call a thorough beating…”; then JUSTIFY / SORRY.

options.label: LOSE
options.effect: Carl: “Are your circuits rusty? Or are you just taking pity on an old man?”; then LIE / TRUTH.

options.label: DRAW
options.effect: Carl: “That is a very odd draw…”; then LIE / TRUTH.

decisions.note: Chart sub-group; all three complete on the chart together (PowerPyx).

benchmark.note: A decision with the template’s prompt; stored as painterPastime. No stat change.

decisions.title: After the chess game
decisions.context: The template’s follow-up prompts: after WIN, JUSTIFY (“you don’t like when I let you win”) or SORRY (“I prefer humiliation to pity”); after LOSE, LIE or TRUTH (Carl: “Never throw a match, Markus. If you can win, win.”); after DRAW, LIE (“You don’t lie as good as you play chess”) or TRUTH (“A draw feels like an honorable compromise, no?”).

benchmark.note: Three decisions, one per result, gated on painterPastime. No stat change.

decisions.title: Read a book
decisions.context: Carl: “What are you reading?” Plato’s Republic (“Asking questions that have no answers is part of being human”), Macbeth (“Life without emotions wouldn’t be worth living”) or Keats’ Odes (“There’s nothing like love to make a man feel miserable”).
decisions.note: Chart sub-group; the template has three conditioned conversations and no prompt.

benchmark.note: A decision with the game’s interaction labels (Plato, Shakespeare, Keats’ Odes) in chart order; Carl’s answer goes to Markus’s knowledge; stored as painterPastime. No stat change.

decisions.title: Play the piano
decisions.context: Markus chooses a piece; Carl: “Something has changed in the way you play… Sometimes I think you have more humanity than most humans…”
decisions.note: Chart sub-group and the game’s choice group (CHOICEGROUP01). Tempo controls are gameplay, not a prompt.

benchmark.note: A decision with the four moods; Carl’s line goes to Markus’s knowledge; stored as painterPastime. No stat change.

decisions.title: Take Carl to the studio
decisions.context: Carl: “One day, I won’t be here to take care of you anymore… Decide who you are, and wanna become… This world doesn’t like those who are different, Markus. Don’t let anyone tell you who you should be. Let’s go to the studio.” Markus removes the sheet; Carl finishes his painting.

options.label: Scripted, no choice
options.effect: Main-line node; objective REMOVE SHEET. Cleaning the studio is optional and not on the chart.

benchmark.note: A narrated event; Carl’s speech is a fact. No stat change.

decisions.title: Carl’s verdict
decisions.context: Carl: “So… What’s your verdict, Markus?” Whatever the answer: “The truth is I have nothing left to say anymore… Let’s see if you have any talent!”

options.label: LIKE
options.effect: “Something I can’t… quite define. I guess I like it.”

options.label: DON’T LIKE
options.effect: “I don’t think it’s your best work…”

decisions.note: Template prompt, not a chart node; no effect.

benchmark.note: A decision with the template’s labels. No stat change.

decisions.title: Paint Something You See
decisions.context: Markus paints a copy of what he sees. Carl: “That is a perfect copy, of reality. But painting is not about replicating the world, it’s about interpreting it, improving on it, showing something you see.”
decisions.note: Chart node and choice group; in game the buttons read “Paint Carl’s painting”, “Paint desk”, “Paint statue” (objective FIND A SUBJECT TO PAINT).

benchmark.note: A decision with the game’s button labels in chart order; stored as painterCopy; Carl’s critique is a fact. No stat change.

decisions.title: Leo intruded to ask for money (ending)
decisions.context: Carl, at Markus’s painting: “Oh my God…” Leo walks in and asks for cash; Carl refuses (“you’re on it again, aren’t you?”). Leo: “You’d rather take care of your plastic toy here than your own son… This thing is not your son. IT’S A FUCKING MACHINE!” He shoves Markus; Carl: “ENOUGH!” Leo: “You never loved me.” He storms out.

options.label: Scripted, no choice
options.effect: The only ending; leads to Broken.

decisions.note: The chapter’s only ending, no icon (“This chapter has only one outcome”).
